D. Cross-linking of DNA

The patient is experiencing a common side effect related to chemotherapy drugs, particularly those used in the treatment of cancers such as bladder cancer. One classic group of chemotherapeutic agents are the platinum-based compounds, such as cisplatin, which are frequently used in treating various carcinomas including transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder. Cisplatin is known to cause sensorineural hearing loss as a side effect, primarily through its ototoxic effects.

The primary mechanism by which cisplatin and similar drugs exert their anti-cancer effects is by forming cross-links in DNA. This cross-linking inhibits DNA replication and transcription, leading to cell death, especially in rapidly dividing cells such as cancer cells. Despite the therapeutic benefits, the resultant damage is not exclusive to cancer cells, which explains the side effects such as hearing loss due to damage to sensory cells in the ear.
